Hebbian learning published in 'The Organization of Behavior: A Neuropsychological Theory' (1949), Wiley. Year precision. The learning rule 'cells that fire together wire together' is from this monograph.

Wikipedia: Rosenblatt simulated perceptron on IBM 704 in 1957. Key 1958 paper: 'The perceptron: A probabilistic model for information storage and organization in the brain', Psychological Review 65(6):386-408. Term coined at least by 1957 report 'The Perceptron—a perceiving and recognizing automaton'.
Term 'perceptron' appears in Rosenblatt's 1957 Cornell Aeronautical Laboratory report title. Wikipedia Mark I Perceptron publicly demonstrated June 23, 1960.

Fukushima, K. (1980). 'Neocognitron: A self-organizing neural network model for a mechanism of pattern recognition unaffected by shift in position'. Biological Cybernetics 36(4):193-202. Month-year precision (April 1980). An earlier Japanese version appeared in Trans. IECE October 1979.

Minsky & Papert 'Perceptrons', MIT Press, 1969. The XOR/parity impossibility proof for single-layer perceptrons. Key publication that triggered neural-net winter #1. A 1988 expanded edition added prologue/epilogue addressing the revival.

source.title: Group method of data handling — Wikipedia

notes: Wikipedia: GMDH originated 1968 by Ivakhnenko at Institute of Cybernetics, Kyiv. Key 1971 paper: 'Polynomial theory of complex systems', IEEE Trans. Systems Man Cybernetics. 8-layer net trained as early as 1971 (per Schmidhuber's citation). Note: the specimen says 1965; Schmidhuber sources cite 1965 (Cybernetic Predicting Devices book). Wikipedia says 1968. Holding at 0.78 due to discrepancy.

Wikipedia: 'Modern backpropagation was first published by Seppo Linnainmaa as reverse mode of automatic differentiation (1970)'. Year precision. Werbos's 1974 first application to neural networks in his Harvard PhD thesis 'Beyond Regression: New Tools for Prediction and Analysis in the Behavioral Sciences'.

Rumelhart, Hinton, Williams: first 1985 paper, then 1986 Nature paper. Wikipedia: 'published the algorithm first in a 1985 paper, then in a 1986 Nature paper'. The PDP volumes (Rumelhart & McClelland eds., 1986) are the standard citation. Year precision.

LeNet demonstrated 1989 (LeCun et al.). LeNet-5 canonical 1998 paper: LeCun, Bottou, Bengio, Haffner, 'Gradient-based learning applied to document recognition', Proc. IEEE 86(11):2278-2324. Deployed reading checks commercially from June 1996; processing ~20M checks/day by 2001.

Hopfield network paper 1982 (Hopfield, PNAS). Boltzmann machine: Ackley, Hinton, Sejnowski, 'A Learning Algorithm for Boltzmann Machines', Cognitive Science 9(1):147-169, 1985. The spin-glass physics bridge via Sherrington-Kirkpatrick 1975 predates this but is the physical root.
Hinton, Osindero, Teh: 'A fast learning algorithm for deep belief nets', Neural Computation 18(7):1527-1554, July 2006. Month-year precision.

AlexNet submitted to ILSVRC September 30, 2012. Top-5 error 15.3%, winning by >10.8% margin. Authors: Krizhevsky, Sutskever, Hinton (team SuperVision, Univ. Toronto). Two GTX 580 GPUs (3GB each). Formal paper published Communications of the ACM May 2017.

Wikipedia: 'initial CUDA SDK became available on 15 February 2007, for Microsoft Windows and Linux.' NVIDIA hired Ian Buck 2004 paired with John Nickolls; ~3 years development. Day-precision from Wikipedia.
ImageNet first presented as poster at CVPR 2009. Fei-Fei Li began work in 2006. Full public release Fall 2011. First ILSVRC competition 2010. Year of first public presentation = 2009.

source.title: Attention Is All You Need — Wikipedia

notes: 'Attention Is All You Need', Vaswani et al., arXiv:1706.03762, published June 12, 2017. NeurIPS 2017. 8 Google authors. As of 2025: over 173,000 citations, top ten most-cited papers of 21st century.

Wikipedia: term 'deep learning' introduced to machine learning by Rina Dechter in 1986, then applied to artificial neural networks by Igor Aizenberg and colleagues in 2000. The Hinton-era 'deep learning' as a field label solidified ~2006. Certainty 0.65: Wikipedia gives two dates (1986 ML context, 2000 ANN context); the 2006 Hinton revival is when the modern usage crystallized but that is the sw-dbn node.

notes: ChatGPT released November 30, 2022 by OpenAI. 100M users milestone within ~2 months. Consumer-facing consummation of the deep-learning lineage per specimen description.

ESTIMATE: theory-DNA basis. Connectionist substrate (W_A) contribution share to the deep learning weld. Roughly equal weighting with optimization/gradient (W_B) acknowledged in most historiographies; the architecture is the substrate but the breakthrough required both parents equally. Proxy: historical accounts treat the two ancestral parents as roughly co-equal. Certainty capped at 0.4 (historiographic estimate, no explicit quantification found). Basis: standard deep learning histories treat backprop + neural nets as co-equal contributors.

ESTIMATE: theory-DNA basis. Optimization/gradient descent (W_B) contribution share. Roughly co-equal to W_A; backpropagation is often cited as THE key breakthrough (Rumelhart et al. 1986 often called 'the paper' of the revival). Some historians weight this higher (the algorithm solved the previously unsolvable hidden-layer training problem). Certainty capped at 0.4.

ESTIMATE: theory-DNA for GPU compute as gating instrument-parent. AlexNet explicitly used 2 GTX 580 GPUs; Fei-Fei Li quote 'three elements converged'. The compute instrument is the rate-limiting parent that held up the weld from 1986 to 2012 (~26 years). Assigned 0.3 share recognizing it as gating but instrumental (not an idea-parent). Certainty 0.35 (historiographic estimate).

ESTIMATE: theory-DNA for ImageNet as data instrument-parent. Fei-Fei Li's three-element framing gives data co-equal footing with compute in the consummation, but the algorithm and optimization ideas are more foundational across the field's history. Assigned 0.25 share. Certainty 0.35 (historiographic estimate).

Symbolic AI as rival: dominant through 1980s expert systems era, decisively displaced as dominant paradigm by deep learning post-2012. Persists as a niche (neuro-symbolic hybrids, formal verification, knowledge graphs). Not fully absorbed, not fully faded. Specimen confirms 'displaced rather than fused'. Fate: niche (persists in specialized domains).

Symbolics/Lisp Machines Inc. commercial arm of symbolic AI: Wikipedia 'An entire industry worth half a billion dollars was replaced in a single year [1987].' Symbolics bankrupt ~1987 (formal Wikidata dissolution 1996). Rival fate: faded (the commercial Lisp-machine industry collapsed entirely).
Japan's Fifth Generation project concluded 1994 in 'commercial failure'; specialized hardware outperformed by general-purpose systems. Rival state bet: faded (project ended, goals unmet).

value: The Perceptrons book (1969) caused approximately 17-year publication/adoption lag in multi-layer neural network research; major groups abandoned the area from ~1969 until backprop revival 1986
notes: D6 friction: documented gatekeeping / adoption lag. Minsky-Papert theorem + MIT prestige redirected funding away from neural nets. AI winter #1 start 1974 per Wikipedia (Lighthill-triggered broadly), but neural-net-specific squeeze began ~1969. Estimated ~17-year adoption lag for multi-layer nets.

value: LeNet deployed reading bank checks June 1996 but deep learning did not become dominant paradigm until 2012 — approximately 23-year lag from 1989 demonstration to paradigm adoption
notes: D6 friction / demonstrated-not-adopted gap. Wikipedia: LeNet deployed commercially June 1996 (NCR systems in bank back offices). By 2001 processing ~20M checks/day. Yet deep learning paradigm adoption awaited 2012 (AlexNet). The 'demonstrated-not-adopted' case the specimen highlights.
